names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 februarie.
Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 14 iulie, «Sfântul Apostol Achila», with the rank word left off; the life page spells him «Acvila» in its prose.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Φεβρουαρίου, «Άγιοι Ακύλας και Πρίσκιλλα οι Απόστολοι», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 14. јул ст. ст., „Св. апостол Акила.“ — „Св.“ is not a rank and „апостол“ is the rank `types` already carries, so the bare forename is the whole form; the heading gives no by-name, no see and no place. `foldchk.py` returns **no holder** and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder — which is a surprise worth recording, the corpus holding four Aquila folders, because none of the other three stores a Serbian form. **The string therefore folds with nobody while the day-number collides with `aquila-14-july` exactly**, and the two facts are independent: a fold is a name and a collision is a day.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

feast.note: doxologia.ro also keeps him on 14 iulie, «Sfantul Apostol Achila», with a life of its own and a troparion; that page and this one are the same man -- the Jew of Pontus, the tent-maker, the husband of Priscilla, driven from Rome by Claudius and baptised by Paul (read 24 September 2026). One row per church is the schema, so the second day is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 februarie — «Sfinți Apostoli și Mucenici Acvila și soția sa, Priscila»

attestations.note: The page closes with a second day for him alone: «O Άγιος Aκύλας εορτάζεται και στις 14 Ιουλίου» — Aquila is kept also on 14 July. One attestation row is one feast, so the row records the day read and the second day stands here as a note; the page gives Priscilla no second day.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.07.2026 (14. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. апостол Акила.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. **THE DAY-NUMBER MATCHES A DIFFERENT MAN EXACTLY, AND THAT IS THIS ENTRY’S WHOLE DIFFICULTY.** `aquila-14-july` is a folder of this corpus, display name «Aquila (14 July)», a `martyr` kept **venerated by the Greek calendar on the 14 July** — the very number this book prints — with a companion `hilarius-companion-of-aquila` and an `undocumented` `serbian` row standing empty and ready. A reader matching on the day would have written this entry onto him, and it would have been the worst failure this job has. **He is not the man.** His whole source is saint.gr’s 14 Ιουλίου line «Άγιοι Ακύλας και Ιλάριος» and one sentence behind it: the two were martyred by stoning, and «Δεν έχουμε άλλες λεπτομέρειες για τους βίους τους», we have no other details of their lives — no year, no place, no emperor, no judge, no apostleship and no wife. This entry is a dossier: one of the Seventy; a Jew who lived first in Italy with his wife Priscilla; Claudius’s expulsion of the Jews from Rome and Italy; the move to Corinth; the apostle Paul’s year and a half in his house and the baptism of him and his wife; the journey with Paul as far as Ephesus; **three epistles quoted by chapter and verse**; the work at Ephesus with Timothy; and a bishopric. **And the identification is confirmed by the other calendar in this folder’s own life**: saint.gr’s page for the couple, read on 30 September 2026 and already written into the closing paragraph of `aquila`’s life, says in so many words that **Aquila is kept again on 14 July**. So the Greek calendar keeps the apostle twice, on the 13 February and the 14 July, and keeps a bare line for an Aquila and a Hilarius on the second of those days as well. This book keeps the apostle on the 14 July. The row goes where the dossier goes. **Whether the Greek 14 July line and the apostle are one man is a question this reading does not answer and does not need to**: `aquila-14-july` is left exactly as it stands, with its `serbian` row still `undocumented`, and the question is for the author. **THREE ROWS IN FEBRUARY AND THIS ONE IN JULY.** The folder’s Romanian and Greek rows both stand on the **13 February**, and this book keeps him on the **14 July** — a different month and a different number, which is neither a thirteen-day conversion nor a near miss. The `serbian` row was `undocumented`, so it is written plainly on this book’s day and **nothing of the other two is touched** — §4 forbids moving a principal day — and the two days stand side by side in the life, as they do on `pancratius-of-tauromenium` from 9 July and `golinduhia-of-persia` from 12 July. **`dates` STAY NULL.** The folder holds none and this book gives no year, no century and no reign for his death: he was at last killed by embittered pagans and passed over into the kingdom of Christ. **The one emperor it names is a date and is not his**: Claudius ordered the Jews expelled from Rome and Italy, and after Claudius’s death they were allowed to return — a reign twice over, and a reign is no source for a year. `types` UNTOUCHED at `apostle`, `bishop` and `martyr`: „апостол“ is the `apostle`, „Један од седамдесет апостола“ confirms which seventy, „Као епископ Акила многе крсти“ is the `bishop`, and „би убијен од озлобљених незнабожаца“ is the `martyr` — **all three of the folder’s types are earned by this entry and not one of them is new**, which is the first time in this range that a heading and a body have between them confirmed every word a folder held. No `office`: the book gives him the rank of bishop and **no see**, and an `office` string is not invented from Ephesus or anywhere else. No `locations`: Italy, Rome, Corinth and Ephesus are a narrative. **ONE RELATED ROW ALREADY EXISTS AND NO NEW ONE IS MADE.** `priscilla` is related in both directions already and is his wife throughout the entry, so the life links her. **The apostle Paul and the apostle Timothy take no row**: Paul is the man who first came to know him at Corinth, lodged in his house a year and a half, baptised him and his wife, and greeted him by name in three epistles, which is as close to this man’s story as another apostle can get — and the rule is still that an identification made off a name in another man’s life is not an identification and that a `related` row is a reading. The prose names them as the book does, «the apostle Paul» and «Timothy», which are not the display names of `paul-the-apostle` or of any Timothy folder. Claudius is an emperor. **WHAT IS NEW IS THREE EPISTLES CITED BY CHAPTER AND VERSE**, which no other calendar in this folder does: the first to the Corinthians, written by Paul from Ephesus, «greet you much Aquila and Priscilla with the church in their house» — the book gives it as 16, 9; the Romans, written from Corinth, «greet Priscilla and Aquila, my helpers in Christ Jesus, who laid down their own necks for my soul, to whom not I only give thanks but all the churches of the nations, and their house church», 16, 3-4; and the second to Timothy, written in chains at Rome, «greet Priscilla and Aquila», II Tim. 4, 19. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **ENTRY 2 IS AN EGYPTIAN MONK AND THE NEAREST NAME ALREADY HAS A SERBIAN ROW ON ANOTHER DAY, WHICH IS TWO REFUSALS IN ONE.** „Преп. Елије.“ — „Монах Мисирски из IV столећа“, an Egyptian monk of the fourth century. `ls saints | grep -i "^elias\|^elijah\|^helle"` turns up `elias-the-egyptian` and nothing nearer — and **he is a `martyr` of Caesarea in Palestine, one of the twelve beheaded under Firmilianus, who already carries a venerated `serbian` row on the 16 February** off this very book, which heads that day „Светих дванаест мученика.“ and names him among the five Egyptian brothers. So writing this entry onto him would be both an identification made off a forename and a breach of §1, which is the exact pair of refusals Isaiah the hermit of Scetis took on 3 July. **No folder from me**, Ruling 3, and the entry is reported here instead: from early youth he gave himself to monastic struggles in the desert, so that by his life and by mighty wonders he drew the wonder of monks and laymen alike, and though he fled from the glory of men he could not hide; he had great battles with the devil’s delusions, especially during a long fast, **the devil setting before him now honey and now beautiful apples**, and he was not deceived; and he saw into men’s hearts and guessed every man’s passion and every man’s thought — „не због тога да би показао своје тајанствено знање него да би људе исправио“, not in order to show his mysterious knowledge but in order to set men right. The fourth century it gives him is a stated century on a folder that does not exist, and nothing can be done with it.

hymns.text: Apostole sfinte Achila, roagă pe milostivul Dumnezeu, ca să dăruiască iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Apostol Achila, unul din cei șaptezeci», Glasul 3

english.text: Holy apostle Aquila, pray the merciful God that He grant our souls forgiveness of our offences.

hymns.text: Χριστὸν ἀγαπήσαντες καὶ φωτισθέντες τὸν νοῦν, τὴ πίστει ἐνούμενοι καὶ συζυγία σεμνή, Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρισκίλλα ἤσαν μὲν προεστῶτες ἐκκλησίας κατ’ οἶκον, Παύλου δὲ τοῦ φωστῆρος συνεργοὶ καὶ προστᾶται. Διὸ αὐτοὺς τιμήσωμεν καὶ μιμησώμεθα.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, on the page of Άγιος Ακύλας ο Απόστολος and Αγία Πρίσκιλλα. One hymn for the pair, naming both; the itacism «τὴ πίστει» is the page's own.

english.text: Having loved Christ and been enlightened in mind, united in the faith and in an honourable marriage, Aquila and Priscilla were heads of a church in their own house, and fellow workers and protectors of Paul the light-giver. Therefore let us honour them and imitate them.
